idris Elba

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Idris Elba star of Long walk to Freedom in a candid interview with Bongani Bingwa

Further information:
Idriss Elba Proposal

He is an actor, a producer, a musician and a DJ. He has also been nominated as the sexiest man in Hollywood, but his biggest role to date is most certainly the role of Nelson Mandela in the film: LONG WALK TO FREEDOM, a role he didn’t ever imagine being cast in, he told Carte Blanche

Yet when you were cast u thought it was a joke?
“ I thought it was a joke I said are you sure you mean me and not Morgan Freeman? I think he is available! Because I was like how can you ask Idriss Elba to play Nelson Mandela that doesn’t even make sense!

It was a huge challenge and stretched his technical ability he says

Was there extra pressure because he was an icon?
Totally! The pressure was immense he is a world icon. There is JESUS, ELVIS, MANDELA, everybody know who this man is but it was also an opportunity to create something beautiful about his life – but the idea that I had to make his presence come alive on screen, was very scary

The film debuted in London on the night of Mandela’s death last year, it was according to Idriss Elba one of the strangest and most beautiful nights of my life he says:

Just thinking about it makes me feel quite tearful, because it was the day the world was about to celebrate the man in film form and I was a part of that. The Royal family was there. It was a BIG day. I had thirty members of my family in the audience and the producers and I decided to go on stage because the audience didn’t know, they were watching the film. We came on stage at the credits and made the announcement. Everybody gasped,
people were in tears, I mean honestly the whole auditorium including the royal family just sat in silence

Idriss was recently in South Africa to promote his new album called Mi Mandela

Mi Mandela spelt M.I is partly where my parents are from Sierra Leone they speak Creole and you say Namiose which means that this is my home but it also means this is your home in other words namios- you can have this as well, so mi Mandela means Mandela for all of u or all of us.

Last year this 6.3 gentle man was voted one of the sexiest men alive but despite the adulation it is his father’s approval that has meant everything to him. When Idriss Elba speaks of his dad he still gets emotional

“I showed my dad the very early cut of this film, he went with his brother and my mom and they had a cinema to themselves, and my dad cried he was just very proud that this was his boy….. my dad was a union man, and he cried as he watched it …sorry man I didn’t want to get emotional

Press Release:


Idris Elba
Madiba never had a chance to see the final cut of the film ‘Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom’ - he died at the age of 95 on December 5th 2013, the very day that the film premiered in London. Now, British actor Idris Elba speaks candidly to Carte Blanche about everything from becoming Mandela to play his part in the film, to how the press and members of the Mandela and British Royal families attending the premiere, found out that the global icon had passed away.


Script:


IDRIS ELBA FINAL SCRIPT

Commentary One
He is an actor, producer, singer, and DJ, but South Africans best know Idris Elba as the man who took on the role of Nelson Mandela in the movie, Long Walk to Freedom.

Up sound movie car chase

But when he got the casting call, he thought it was a mistake

Up sound Mandela: Some body want me?

Bongani
When you were cast you thought it was a joke

Idris
I thought it was a joke! (Laughs) I said are you sure you mean me and not Morgan Freeman? I think he is available! Because I was like how can you ask Idris Elba to play Nelson Mandela that doesn’t even make sense! But my agent who is also South African and lives in London said no man this is serious…seriaars he said!

Commentary Two
Idris says he has fallen in love with South Africa – he has just released an album as a tribute to Mandela,

Up sound “ When nothing seems positive…”

Commentary Three
But there was a time he was skeptical about the country

Up sound music

Idris
If I am honest I came to SA with some prejudice and a little bit of animosity as to what happened here. I was completely turned on my head when I got here. Unlike anywhere I have been in the world you know, this country just made me feel very welcome

Up sound wedding

Commentary Three
The movie had the blessing of Mandela, but he never saw the final product. Last year South African audiences embraced it

Idris
I felt that we really put SA film making on the world stage in a massive way and I felt that very proud of that

Commentary Four
But how does one begin preparing for the role of an international icon?

Up sound Movie
Let them try!

Idris
JESUS, ELVIS, MANDELA, everybody knows who this man is! The pressure was immense. The idea that I had to make his presence come alive on screen was very scary

Up Sound movie: Freedom – it is an ideal for which I am prepared to die

Commentary Five changed
It was Idris big presence that that attracted the producer and director, but he also put in, a lot of hard work

Amandla!

Idris
I read as much as I could and then I came to SA and travelled SA as much as I could. I went the Eastern Cape to Quunu. I visited his family, his friends, people that he knew, I took journeys that he may have took, I listened to music he would I listened to, I studied his timbre – I had to mask this London accent and put this very famous voice on. That is the most work I have done for any character

Up sound: I do not deny that I planned sabotage I did not plan it in a spirit of ….nor because I have any love for violence

Commentary six
The coming week marks the first anniversary of Nelson Mandela’s death which happened the night the film premiered in London, at a Royal performance

Idris
Just thinking about it man it makes me feel quite tearful. The Royal family was there it was a BIG day! I had almost 30 members of my family in the audience and the producers the directors and I decided to go on stage, because the audience didn’t know and we came on stage at the credits and made the announcement, and you could hear, I mean everybody gasped. I mean honestly the whole auditorium including the royal family just sat in silence

Commentary Seven
Mandela’s death came only three months after the death of his own father Winston Elba
Bongani
What would your dad have made of all of this success?
Idris
I showed my dad the very early cut of this film, and he went with his brother and my mom and they had a cinema to themselves and my dad cried. He cried, he was just very proud…sorry that this was his boy – my dad was very into Mandela, he was union man and he always refer to Mandela would do this ….and he just cried and watched it …yeah man

Up sound music

Commentary eight
During the filming of Mandela, Idris also discovered South African music

Idris
I was surprised how diverse the music is from house to hip hop, to traditional and how many different sounds were coming from South Africa, and I also feel the world needs to hear more

Commentary nine
It has all cuIminated in an album he has curated, written and produced, called Mi Mandela

Up sound Idris singing: “I flew down to joburg..

Idris
It was like a therapy session, I had a studio for about four weeks and artists would come in and come out, fly in and fly out



Commentary ten
It’s a collaboration of diverse musicians, from Mumford and Sons to the Mahotella Queens

Idris
I just felt like you know, that this album takes a little bit of a hybrid approach to SA music, a mash up

Commentary eleven
As a tribute to Mandela, the cover resembles the cut up letters he received when he was in prison. It’s also a final letter to Idris’s father

Up sound music …you give me love…

Idris
My dad died just before I came to SA to do this record. He loved me as an actor, but he always said go and do your music, I know that you love it, and I wanted to say something to him and I thought about writing him something and the letter is a final goodbye and a hey man I did it – hope you get to like this record.

Commentary Twelve
Despite his good looks and his imposing presence Idris Elba doesn’t understand why he is a sex symbol

Bongani
Now I have to ask you - how are you doing with all the other accolades like being the sexiest man alive or one of the sexiest men alive -how are you dealing with that?

Idris
I LOVE it! You kidding me, no it’s a compliment of course but it surprises me, I look at this face every morning and I think I am not sexy I don’t know how they see me as sexy

Bongani
And then of course there was that mic-wire incident ….
Idris laughs

Commentary thirteen
These photos of an apparently well-endowed Idris went viral on Twitter, but he always maintained he’d left a microphone in his pocket.

Idris
Rumour has it! … let’s leave it at that…

Bongani
But how do you deal with all that? The whole world is discussing your bulge?

Idris
You know it was on CNN I think it made CNN tickertape…I think the world is just fascinated with size

Bongani
Ok we will leave it at that then….they laugh.

Commentary fourteen
This week South Africans will honour the legacy left behind by one of the world’s great statesman

Up sound: I Nelson Mandela

Idris
From a world- wide perspective I feel he is very very much missed. This Ebola crisis that is happening in West Africa, if Madiba was alive I can imagine that he would motivate the rest of Africa in a way that no one else can!

Bongani
As much as the world venerates Madiba have we think that as much as the world venerates Mandela, have we learnt enough about what he stood for to do the things he would want us to do?

Idris
I think his teachings have definitely left an imprint on the country, I think you can sense that everybody wants to keep his legacy alive. But it’s up to us now.

THE END 09 minutes
